$comment: Prose for the deterministic text-slug stubs (bin/lib/llm-text-stubs.ts; GRND-19, D-18-06). Used only under PENSMITH_NO_LLM=1 / --dry-run and as the RUN-21 mock LLM's default text replies. {name} marks a value the stub fills in; every other character is emitted as written. The drafter prose never quotes (no double quotes, no block quotes) and cites only through the {cite} / {cites} slots, which the stub fills with [@citekey] tokens of the section's assigned sources.

section-drafter.opening_with_topic: This section, {title}, develops one part of the paper's account of {topic}.
section-drafter.opening: This section, {title}, develops one part of the paper's argument.
cited: Prior work examined here offers direct evidence for the point at hand {cite}.
A related study extends the argument and clarifies where its conclusions apply {cite}.
Further evidence qualifies this reading and marks the limits of the claim {cite}.
One account in the literature frames the problem in the terms the rest of the section adopts {cite}.
The findings of another source support the same conclusion from a different direction {cite}.
A later analysis tests the claim against new cases and reports where it holds {cite}.
section-drafter.cited_group: Several sources inform this part of the argument {cites}.
filler: The section develops this point in steps, so that each claim can be checked against its source.
It first states the claim, then sets out the reasoning that connects it to the evidence.
Where the evidence is partial, the text says so rather than overstating the case.
The argument keeps to what the assigned sources can support.
Each step builds on the one before it and prepares the next.
Terms are used in the same sense as in the rest of the paper.
Counterexamples are acknowledged where they bear on the claim.
This keeps the section focused on its purpose within the paper.
The reasoning stays explicit so a reader can follow it.
Open questions are named rather than passed over.
section-drafter.closing: The next section takes up the argument from this point.

revise-swap.rationale: No model was called (LLM stubbed), so the flagged citation is removed mechanically rather than replaced.

tutorial-section-provenance.with_claim: **{citekey}**: cited for the claim that {claim}. Check that the source reports this finding directly, and note its scope before relying on it.
tutorial-section-provenance.without_claim: **{citekey}**: assigned to this section, but no claim cites it yet. Find the claim it supports, or drop it from the section.
tutorial-section-provenance.none: No sources are assigned to this section, so there is no evidence trail to explain yet.

tutorial-research-rationale.per_source: **{citekey}**: selected as evidence on {topic}. Name the specific facet of the topic it will support, and note what it leaves uncovered.
tutorial-research-rationale.coverage: Before writing, check which facet of the topic the set as a whole still leaves under-supported.
tutorial-research-rationale.none: The working bibliography is empty, so there are no sources to explain yet.

humanizer.$comment: The humanizer stub (EXP-14) rewrites prose deterministically: each [from, to] pair replaces the whole word or phrase `from` (case kept on the first letter) in every prose paragraph; headings, block quotes and placeholder tokens are never touched. A section with none of these words gets the fallback prefix on its first prose paragraph instead, so the stubbed text always differs.
